senses.gloss:
Stanayitnu, sing. and plur., denotes ‘thunder’ from the
Rigveda^1 onwards.^2
1) v. 83, 6.
2) Av. i. 13, 1; iv. 15, 11; vii. 11, 1, etc.

Stamba in the Atharvaveda^1 and later^2 denotes a ‘tuft of
grass,’ or more generally a ‘bunch’ or ‘cluster.’
1) viii. 6, 14.
2) Taittirīya Saṃhitā, v. 6, 4, 1 (of
Darbha); Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa, ii. 7,
17, 3; iii. 2, 2, 4; 3, 3, 4; Aitareya
Brāhmaṇa, v. 23, 9, etc.

Stambha, ‘pillar,’ is found in the Kāṭhaka Saṃhitā,^1 and
often in the Sūtras. Earlier Skambha^2 is used, but only
metaphorically.
1) xxx. 9; xxxi. 1.
2) Rv. i. 34, 2; iv. 13, 5, etc.

Starī denotes a ‘barren cow’ in the Rigveda (i. 101, 3;
116, 22; 117, 20, etc.).
